notes:
Independent review by Claude Code, session cc-fb70e5, 23 September 2026, of the extraction by session cc-7b31c4 (issue #1428). cc-fb70e5 appears nowhere in its files.

Provenance. The recorded hash matches byte for byte: the arXiv v2 PDF, 0139fc5a...91a5f2 (51 pp.). I also took the v2 e-print (FL.tex, 3126 lines) and checked every quotation there. I independently reproduced the extraction's report that the published version is unreachable: both doi.org/10.1090/jams/948 and the AMS article page return HTTP 403. So the locators are against arXiv v2, as recorded, and neither the extraction nor this review can speak for the journal text - which matters here, because the companion paper's extraction found that the journal version of that paper differs substantively from its preprint.

Numbering and coverage. Seventeen environments share one per-section counter, and the appendix letters it. My first simulation counted commented-out environments in the source and gave 171 objects with shifted numbers; stripping comments first gives 154, and that is the numbering the extraction uses. Every number I tested against it agrees: thm:volume = Theorem 2.21 (the extraction's item 5 says '= Theorem 2.21, p. 13'), situation:locally_quotient = Situation 2.6, defi:weight = Definition 2.20, and the four findings' locators (Construction 2.13, Remark 6.19, Goal 6.21, Remark 6.24) all land on the right environment. Coverage: 150 of the 154 objects appear in an item locator. The four that do not are Situation 2.3, Situation 4.24 (Donagi-Gaitsgory, whose content is in three item statements by name), Remark 4.33 and Goal 6.21 (which the findings cite). No gap worth recording.

Statuses. The four library items were read in the source at the pins: MeasureTheory.Measure.haarMeasure, haarMeasure_unique and haarMeasure_self in Mathlib 082e2d3 (MeasureTheory/Measure/Haar/Basic.lean), AddCircle.toCircle with toCircle_add and toCircle_apply_mk (Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Complex/Circle.lean:380, inside namespace AddCircle), CategoryTheory.Abelian.DoldKan.equivalence and CategoryTheory.Idempotents.DoldKan.equivalence (AlgebraicTopology/DoldKan/Equivalence.lean:168-169), and TauCeti.subsingleton_brauerGroup_of_finite at Tau Ceti f790474 (TauCeti/Algebra/BrauerGroup/Trivial.lean:247). The 20 planned items and the routes cite 12 layers between them; all 12 exist in data/atlas.json.

Routes. One Part II and three source routes, all accepted; see the route verdicts.

Mistakes in the paper. All four recorded findings are confirmed, each verbatim in the source. E4 deserves a note: Goal 6.21(1) and (2) carry the same pointer, and the argument for (2) is in the deferred 'Proof of Lemma 6.14' printed after the proof of Lemma 6.34 - a line-order check misattributes it, and the extraction read the structure correctly.

Two findings added. All four recorded findings are mis-citations of the kind 'cited as Theorem, printed as Proposition'. I audited that class mechanically - for every reference of the form '<word>~\ref{label}' in the source, compare the word with the environment carrying the label - and the paper has five such mismatches, of which the extraction recorded three. The two it missed are now E5 (the section 2 overview calls Lemma 2.8, the existence of the canonical measure, 'Definition 2.8'; the paper itself cites it as 'Lemma 2.8' in section 6) and E6 (section 6.3 calls Construction 2.13 'Definition 2.13'; the paper cites it correctly as a Construction at four other places). Both are misprints affecting nothing, and both are settled by the paper against itself. The same audit found no duplicate labels and no undefined references.

The lesson for the register: when an extraction's findings all belong to one mechanical class, the reviewer's job is to run that class exhaustively rather than re-check the instances one by one.

Verdict: accept.
